chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The nobility of the Believer is standing at night (for prayer), and his honour is his self-sufficiency from the people.

key_terms.قِيَامُ اللَّيْلِ: Night prayer / standing in prayer at night

ai.seo_question: What are the sources of a believer's nobility and honour according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi elevates qiyam al-layl as the primary marker of spiritual nobility, reflecting the belief that nocturnal devotion strengthens the soul's connection to the Divine. Simultaneously, it frames istighna (self-sufficiency) not merely as financial independence, but as a dignified state of not being burdened by or dependent upon others, thereby preserving the believer's honor. This dual emphasis underscores the integration of vertical worship and horizontal social conduct in achieving a complete moral character.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The nobility of the Believer is standing at night (for Salāt), and his honour is his self-sufficiency from the people’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The nobility of the believer is in his worship at night and his honor is in his independence from people.”
